source.title: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus Toxic Shock Syndrome

source_integrity_findings.correction: A May 2005 Emerging Infectious Diseases correction states that this should read C-reactive protein 43.7 mg/dL.
source_integrity_findings.handling: The ATOM set preserves the retrieved raw PDF as written. The correction is recorded here and in SEA as external verification, not silently substituted into the source atom.

source_integrity_findings.finding: The treatment paragraph prints 'teicoplamin'; the final paragraph prints 'teicoplanin'. Both source forms are preserved in separate treatment atoms.
The letter says the MRSA strain produced TSST-1, but the case methods described in the letter report PCR detection of the TSST-1 gene rather than a direct toxin-production assay.

extraction_limitations: This is a two-page letter describing one patient, not a controlled study.
The letter has no formal Methods, Results, or Limitations headings. SourceSection values map the narrative to the closest schema category.
No tables, figures, algorithms, appendices, or supplements are present in the target letter.
Funding, conflict-of-interest, and data-availability statements are not reported in the retrieved letter and were not invented.
Cited studies were not atomized. Secondary claims drawn from cited literature are tagged as secondary reports.
schema_gaps: The LiteratureAtom schema has no dedicated case-report timeline or diagnostic-finding atom kind, so clinical course statements use population_description, qualitative_result, method, or other as appropriate.
The schema has no field for post-publication errata linked to a specific atom. The published correction is therefore recorded in this validation report rather than inserted as source-reported data.

external_verification.purpose: Article identity, DOI, and the published laboratory-value correction were checked against CDC/EID pages. External material did not replace the retrieved PDF for ATOM extraction.
